name: Pere Ubu
label: Rough Trade
lede: David Thomas wanted one Cleveland single to turn up in a thrift-store bin someday. He kept the band going for fifty years instead, through 21 musicians, Rough Trade, MTV and a stage version of the play it's named after.

eras.title: One single, then the band wouldn't stop
eras.text: Rocket from the Tombs fell apart in the summer of 1975. David Thomas and Peter Laughner put a new band together just to record one Rocket song, and found a sound built from a synthesizer, a steel city and the Velvet Underground.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pere Ubu · NPR · The Guardian: David Thomas
years.h: Thomas and Laughner name a band after Alfred Jarry's tyrant
years.p: [[David Thomas|b6459915-9b42-477a-aa17-fdcae9ff2d13]] and [[Peter Laughner|fb3391e5-9006-4cc6-89ae-46b9aff3b8ee]] recruit Tom Herman, Tim Wright, Scott Krauss and synth player Allen Ravenstine. Père Ubu is the monstrous king of Jarry's 1896 play Ubu Roi.
years.xp:
Thomas had been Crocus Behemoth, art director and gossip columnist at the Cleveland Scene, and sang in the Great Bow-Wah Death Band. He told the Guardian Rocket from the Tombs never kept a drummer longer than three months. Cheetah Chrome went on to the Dead Boys.

Several of the band lived in the Plaza Apartments, 3206 Prospect Avenue, a downtown building Ravenstine owned and filled with artists.

q: I just wanted to leave something behind.
years.h: 30 Seconds Over Tokyo, aimed at a future thrift-store bin
years.p: The first single, on their own Hearpen label, is a Doolittle Raid song named after the 1944 film; Conrad's Heart of Darkness is on the flip. It was meant to be the only release.
years.xp: Thomas wanted somebody to find it in a Salvation Army bin ten years on and wonder who this Cleveland band was. Introducing them that month in the Plain Dealer, Jane Scott wrote: "They may never be accepted by the general public. They don't care."

years.h: New Year's Eve is the first show
years.p: Pere Ubu plays live for the first time on the last night of 1975, after the single is already out.

years.cap: Pere Ubu at the Pirate's Cove, Cleveland, c. 1976
years.src: Wikipedia: Pere Ubu · Wikipedia: Peter Laughner
years.h: Final Solution, and Peter Laughner is out
years.p: Hearpen's second single, backed with Cloud 149. Laughner, drinking hard and abusing other substances, leaves soon after.
years.xp: Bandmates had worried about his reliability. Laughner joined the writing staff at Creem alongside Lester Bangs.

years.h: A Mercury A&R man finds Street Waves in a record store
years.p: Cliff Burnstein hears the third single and signs the band to Blank, a Mercury imprint he's building. Tim Wright leaves for New York's [[DNA|97cecdca-af46-4344-9677-ed80bfe43b66]]; Tony Maimone takes bass.

eras.title: Avant-garage on a major's dime
eras.text: Mercury money bought 24 tracks and the band filled them with breaking glass and synthesizer noise engineers took for a fault. Two albums in 1978 made them critics' heroes on both sides of the Atlantic, and sold poorly.

years.h: Peter Laughner dies at 24
years.p: The founding guitarist dies of acute pancreatitis, after years of heavy drug and alcohol use.
years.xp: A letter he mailed the night before said he planned to go to rural Ohio to write and get his health back.

years.h: Anton Fier takes over the drums from Scott Krauss
years.p: [[Anton Fier|9e6becc4-6b97-4649-a37a-256b8f831198]], later of The Feelies, drums with Ubu into 1978. A 1977 tape from Max's Kansas City in New York became Manhattan in Fire's 2015 box.

years.cap: Pere Ubu at the Agora, Cleveland, c. 1977
years.h: Jon Savage needs a new word for Ohio and coins "post-punk"
years.p: Writing in Sounds about Devo, Pere Ubu and a set of British bands, Savage uses the term post-punk for what's coming next.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Modern Dance · The Guardian: David Thomas · Wikipedia: Pere Ubu
years.h: Engineers think Ravenstine's synth is a fault
years.p: Cut at Suma in Painesville with Ken Hamann between 1976 and 1977, the debut is delayed a month because an evangelist already owns the name Dip Records. It flops, and critics adore it.
years.xp:
The studio crew assumed Ravenstine's EML synthesizer was a technical problem until the band convinced them otherwise. The breaking glass on Sentimental Journey was smashed in the studio fireplace. The single mix of The Modern Dance has a doll squeak where the album has a railroad spike.

Rolling Stone later declared modern rock peaked with this album and has declined since. Thomas took it as a challenge.

years.cap: Pere Ubu at the Longhorn, Minneapolis, April 1, 1978
years.h: Johnny Dromette builds a game-show set in the living room
years.p: The Coed Jail! shows with the Suicide Commandos get their name from the set Dromette, Thomas's housemate and record-store manager, built overnight at home.
years.xp: Dromette (John Thompson) made the first Pere Ubu posters and the Datapanik in the Year Zero EP cover, and kept doing their design for decades. The band revived the Coed Jail! name for a 43-date tour in 2016.

years.h: "Look, dub housing": a title from a van window in Baltimore
years.p: Thomas spotted the row of identical Baltimore houses with dub on the van stereo. The cover is the Plaza Apartments, with an extra floor added.
years.xp: Recorded at Suma in August and September 1978 and released on Chrysalis, the album was built as one connected piece. Sounds ranked it 13th of the year, NME later eighth, and Robert Christgau gave it an A. Caligari's Mirror borrows from the shanty Drunken Sailor.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pere Ubu · The Guardian: David Thomas
years.h: Andrew Eldritch calls the F Club show the best gig he ever saw
years.p: Pere Ubu headline the tiny stage at Leeds' F Club with [[The Human League|7adaabfb-acfb-47bc-8c7c-59471c2f0db8]] in support. Eldritch, who'd go on to form [[The Sisters of Mercy|553d8166-27b0-49fe-b8e4-89a984e2c375]], was in the room.
years.xp: On the same UK run, Ian Rankin was at the Edinburgh University show shouting requests at the singer. Decades later the ICU doctor who revived Thomas turned out to have been at that same gig. The band's November 23 set at London's Electric Ballroom was released in 2023 as We Do What We Do.

years.h: After New Picnic Time, Tom Herman quits
years.p: The third album is the founding guitarist's last for 16 years. With Herman gone, Pere Ubu breaks up for the first time.

years.h: Mayo Thompson of the Red Krayola takes the guitar
years.p: [[Mayo Thompson|b463f760-e381-462a-b060-78606b78e5e1]], who toured England with Ubu in 1978, rejoins them for the reformed band. Ubu had already been his backing group on Red Crayola's Soldier-Talk.
years.xp: Ubu Projex dates his arrival to within a month of the band seeing [[Talking Heads|a94a7155-c79d-4409-9fcf-220cb0e4dc3a]] play. Thompson pushed the next record toward abstraction.

eras.title: The Rough Trade years, written in the negative
eras.text: Signed to Rough Trade, a band of Clevelanders and a Texan art-rocker made the most abstract records of their run. The second one fell apart in the studio, and the band went with it.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Art of Walking · Ubu Projex
years.h: "Self-expression is evil," Thomas writes on the control-room wall
years.p: Cut at Suma in January 1980 with Paul Hamann taking over from his father, The Art of Walking is said to have outsold everything Ubu had made before.
years.xp:
On Lost in Art, Krauss and Maimone jammed on keyboards; Thomas answered with drums and vocals in one take and wrote the slogan in the control room. The title came after someone complained they wrote too many songs about driving.

The first US pressing had the wrong mix of Arabia, with a vocal overdub on what should have been an instrumental. Early Rough Trade CDs copied the mistake until the Datapanik remasters fixed it.

years.cap: Pere Ubu in the programme for the spring 1981 UK tour with Gang of Four and Delta 5
years.h: Scott Krauss leaves and Anton Fier comes back
years.p: Fier, the perfectionist from the Feelies, returns for the next album. The live collection 390° of Simulated Stereo, recorded 1976–79, comes out the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Song of the Bailing Man
years.h: Geoff Travis brings in a producer, and the band stops speaking
years.p: That's how Mayo Thompson described himself on Song of the Bailing Man, cut piece by piece with Adam Kidron at Suma. By the end of a late-1982 US tour the members weren't talking.
years.xp: Rough Trade boss Geoff Travis wanted the sessions focused after The Art of Walking. Fier's exacting style collided with Thompson's freeform playing, and everyone except Thomas came away unhappy with the record. Thomas later called it a massively under-recognized achievement.

yt: Birdies, from Urgh! A Music War
years.h: Pere Ubu dissolves again
years.p: Krauss and Maimone start Home and Garden. Thomas goes solo with Richard Thompson and ex-[[Henry Cow|6ba2f6ce-50be-47df-b5a3-298ef032f476]] players, and a filmed Birdies turns up in Urgh! A Music War.

eras.title: Fontana, MTV and Roland Rat
eras.text: A Thomas solo band that was mostly Pere Ubu became Pere Ubu again. On Fontana they made the poppiest records of their life and got as close to the mainstream as they ever would.

years.cap: Pere Ubu in a 1988 Enigma Records press photo
years.h: The solo band turns back into Pere Ubu
years.p: Guitarist Jim Jones and ex-Henry Cow drummer [[Chris Cutler|b8d5c07b-6a7c-4ab7-83b8-8bcc4cb866b6]] join Thomas, Krauss, Maimone and Ravenstine.

years.h: A Fontana deal ends in a TV debut on Roland Rat
years.p: The first album of the new run is the most pop thing they'd made. Their British TV debut came on Roland Rat: The Series.
years.xp: Thomas told the Guardian his only regret about A&R man Dave Bates was that he wasn't more intrusive: Bates was devoted to the band and frightened to mess with them.

years.h: Waiting for Mary hits No. 6 on Modern Rock
years.p: The Cloudland single peaks on Billboard's Modern Rock chart on June 17, 1989 and the video gets on MTV. Love Love Love makes the UK top 100.

yt: What Happened to Me on Night Music, 1989
years.h: Allen Ravenstine leaves and becomes an airline pilot
years.p: Ravenstine and Cutler go after Cloudland. [[Eric Drew Feldman|18bf31b2-1baf-438b-9b64-24c1f2a4eb7d]] takes keyboards for the tour and Worlds in Collision (1991), then leaves for [[Frank Black|98a35a4d-a845-4282-bc7c-5679f2bb9bd2]].

years.cap: Jim Jones, Eric Drew Feldman, Tony Maimone and Pere Ubu
years.h: Tony Maimone leaves for They Might Be Giants
years.p: After Story of My Life, the bassist joins [[They Might Be Giants|183d6ef6-e161-47ff-9085-063c8b897e97]]. Michele Temple comes in and stays for three decades.

years.h: Scott Krauss leaves mid-session and Tom Herman comes home
years.p: Robert Wheeler has taken Ravenstine's synth role, Krauss leaves during the sessions, and Herman returns to tour after a 16-year absence.

eras.title: Movie scores, a Jarry opera and two near-deaths
eras.text: Thomas moved to England, kept a band of long-timers, and pointed Pere Ubu at B-movies, theatre and books about its own records. The illnesses started to cancel tours.

years.h: Wayne Kramer of the MC5 joins for the summer
years.p: Herman plays on Pennsylvania alongside parts from Jim Jones, who'd retired from touring in 1996. Wayne Kramer joins the 1998 summer tour.

years.h: Rocket from the Tombs comes back with Television's Richard Lloyd
years.p: Thomas revives his first band with Cheetah Chrome, Craig Bell, Richard Lloyd and Steve Mehlman for 33 dates. One at Cleveland's Beachland Ballroom is a benefit for the ailing Jim Jones.

years.h: Jim Jones dies at home in Cleveland
years.p: The guitarist from the Fontana years had been around the band from its earliest days and ran its US online store.

years.cap: David Thomas in Bring Me the Head of Ubu Roi, Le Poisson Rouge, New York
years.h: Thomas plays Père Ubu himself at the Southbank
years.p: Bring Me the Head of Ubu Roi, his adaptation of Jarry's play with animations by the Brothers Quay, premieres at Southbank's Ether festival. Sarah Jane Morris plays Mère Ubu.
years.xp: The production was staged again in Poznań in 2009 and the story became the album Long Live Père Ubu! that September. A live recording from the Queen Elizabeth Hall run came out in 2022.

years.cap: Band on the Wall, Manchester, April 2013
years.h: Visas denied, Gagarin plays America by video link from London
years.p: US immigration turns down Keith Moliné and Gagarin for a 17-date tour behind Lady from Shanghai. Cleveland guitarist David Cintron fills in; Gagarin plays some shows on a screen.
years.xp: Lady from Shanghai, named for the Orson Welles noir, came out on Fire on January 7, 2013, with a book about its making modelled on the game Chinese Whispers. Carnival of Souls followed in 2014, grown from the band's live scores to the 1962 horror film.

years.cap: Pere Ubu at the Cobalt, Vancouver, December 2016
years.h: Coed Jail! goes back on the road with Herman picking the songs
years.p: Fire's Architecture of Language box prompts a 43-date tour of material from 1975–82, opening at the Ruby Lounge in Manchester and ending at the Casbah in San Diego.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pere Ubu · The Guardian: David Thomas
years.h: The Long Goodbye gets finished between hospital stays
years.p: Serious illness cancelled the end of the 2017 tour and put him in hospital again after a December 2018 show. The album came out on Cherry Red anyway.
years.xp:
Two days before a December 7, 2018 show in Ramsgate, Gagarin suggested playing the unfinished album in full. The next night's set in Montreuil became a companion disc.

In 2022 Thomas told the Guardian, "I've been dead twice." He had been revived once by an ambulance crew and once woke up in intensive care, where the doctor recognized him from a 1978 Ubu gig.

eras.title: Chaucer, a walker and the last record
eras.text: On dialysis three times a week, Thomas kept writing, remixing and touring short runs. He said his voice had never been better.

q: I expect rock music to be smart.
years.src: The Guardian: David Thomas · Wikipedia: Pere Ubu
years.h: Pere Ubu does The Canterbury Tales in Canterbury
years.p: A one-off at the University of Kent's Gulbenkian theatre, with Bob Holman narrating and Rats on Rafts covering Visions of the Moon.
years.xp: Thomas said he was glad he couldn't jump around any more, because he no longer had to worry about falling into the drums. He'd wanted, from the start, a band William Faulkner or Raymond Chandler would have wanted to join.

years.h: Seventeen songs played for the first time as the tape rolled
years.p: Album 19, produced, mixed and engineered by Thomas, takes its cue from Van Dyke Parks' Song Cycle. The vinyl holds ten tracks; the CD has all 17.

years.h: David Thomas dies at 71 with the MC5 on the radio
years.p: He died of complications from kidney disease. The band's Facebook page said a final album and his autobiography would be published.
